text:
For one mole of an ideal gas, which of these
statements must be true?

(a) U and H each depends only on temperature

(b) Compressibility factor z is not equal to 1

$(c) C_{P, m} – C_{V, m} = R$

$(d) dU = C_{V}dT$ for any process
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An ideal gas has no intermolecular forces, so $U$ depends only on $T$; for one mole $H=U+PV=U+RT$, which also depends only on $T$. The nature of the gas fixes the value of $C_{V}$, not the variables on which $U$ depends. Statement (a) is true.

$PV_{m}=RT$ in every state, so $Z=\dfrac{PV_{m}}{RT}=1$. Statement (b) is false.

$C_{P,m}-C_{V,m}=\dfrac{dH}{dT}-\dfrac{dU}{dT}=\dfrac{d(RT)}{dT}=R$. Statement (c) is true.

Since $U$ depends only on $T$, $dU=\left (\dfrac{𝜕U}{𝜕T}\right )_{V}dT=C_{V}dT$ for any change of the ideal gas, whatever the process. Statement (d) is true.

The true statements are (a), (c) and (d).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
The number of isomers possible for

[$Pt(en)(NO_{2})_{2}$] is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{en})(\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}){}_{2}]$, Pt(II) is square planar. The bidentate en must span two cis positions, so the two nitrite ligands are always cis to each other and there are no geometrical isomers; the molecular plane is a mirror plane, so there are no optical isomers.

$\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ is ambidentate and binds through N (nitro) or through O (nitrito), so the two nitrite ligands can be N,N; N,O; or O,O bonded, giving 3 linkage isomers.


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
The pair in which both the species have the
same magnetic moment (spin only) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Equal spin-only moments, $μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM, need equal numbers of unpaired electrons $n$.

$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{2+}$, $3d^{4}$; weak-field $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ gives $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{1}$, $n=4$.

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$, $3d^{6}$; weak-field $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ gives $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$, $n=4$.

$[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$, $3d^{5}$, high spin, $n=5$.

$[\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$ and $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: tetrahedral $\mathrm{Co}{}^{2+}$, $3d^{7}$, $e^{4}t_{2}^{3}$, $n=3$.

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$, $3d^{6}$; $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is not strong enough to pair the electrons of $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$, so $n=4$ (a low-spin count would be 0), which differs from the 3 of $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$ either way.

The pairs give $n$ = 4 and 3 in (A), 3 and 4 in (B), 5 and 4 in (C), and 4 and 4 in (D).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
[IMG]


$E_{Cu^{2+}|Cu}^{0}$ = +0.34 V

$E_{Zn^{2+}|Zn}^{0}$ = -0.76 V

Identify the incorrect statement from the option
below for the above cell :
options:
If $E_{$ext} < 1.1 V, Zn dissolves at anode and Cu
deposits at cathode

If $E_{$ext} = 1.1 V, no flow of $e^{–}$ or current
occurs
If $E_{$ext$} > 1.1 V, e^{–}$ flows from Cu to Zn

If $E_{$ext} > 1.1 V, Zn dissolves at Zn electrode
and Cu deposits at Cu electrode
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$E_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }=E_{\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}|\mathrm{Cu}}^{\circ }-E_{\mathrm{Zn}{}^{2+}|\mathrm{Zn}}^{\circ }=0.34-(-0.76)=1.10\text{V}$

The external source opposes the cell emf. If $E_{\text{ext}}<1.10\text{V}$, the cell still works as a galvanic cell: Zn dissolves at the anode and Cu deposits at the cathode, so statement (A) is correct.

If $E_{\text{ext}}=1.10\text{V}$, the two emfs balance and no electrons or current flow, so statement (B) is correct.

If $E_{\text{ext}}>1.10\text{V}$, the reaction is reversed and the cell acts as an electrolytic cell: electrons flow from Cu to Zn, Zn is deposited at the zinc electrode and Cu dissolves at the copper electrode. Statement (C) is therefore correct, and statement (D), which says Zn dissolves and Cu deposits, is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
If 75% of a first order reaction was completed
in 90 minutes, 60% of the same reaction would
be completed in approximately (in minutes)
$_______$.

(Take : log 2 = 0.30; log 2.5 = 0.40)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$t_{75$%$} = 90 \min  = 2 × t_{1/2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $t_{1/2} = 45 \min $

Rate constant, K = $\frac{0.693}{45}$ $\min ^{-1}$

Time for completion of 60% of the reaction,

$t_{60$%} = $\frac{2.303}{K}\log \frac{10}{4}$

= $\frac{2.303\times 45}{0.693}\log 2.5$

= 60 min
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
At 300 K, the vapour pressure of a solution
containing 1 mole of n-hexane and 3 moles of
n-heptane is 550 mm of Hg. At the same
temperature, if one more mole of n-heptane is
added to this solution, the vapour pressure of
the solution increases by 10 mm of Hg. What is
the vapour pressure in mm Hg of n-heptane in
its pure state $______$?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $X_{1}$ and P$P_{1}^{o}$
 are the mole fraction and vapour
pressure of n-hexane in solution and $X_{2}$ and $P_{2}^{o}$

 are the mole fraction and vapour pressure of
n-heptane in solution then

550 = $P_{1}^{o}\times\frac{1}{4}$ + $P_{2}^{o}\times\frac{3}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2200 = $P_{1}^{o}$ + 3$P_{2}^{o}$ ....(1)

On addition of 1 more mole of n-heptane

560 = $P_{1}^{o}\times\frac{1}{5}$ + $P_{2}^{o}\times\frac{4}{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2800 = $P_{1}^{o}$ + 4$P_{2}^{o}$ ....(2)

From (1) and (2),

$P_{1}^{o}$ = 400, $P_{2}^{o}$ = 600
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
The mass of ammonia in grams produced when
2.8 kg of dinitrogen quantitatively reacts with 1
kg of dihydrogen is $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$N_{2}(g) + 3H_{2}(g)$ $\to$ $2NH_{3}(g)$

Number of moles of $N_{2} =$ $\frac{2.8\times 10^{3}}{28}$ = 100

Number of moles of $H_{2} =$ $\frac{1000}{2}$ = 500

Here $N_{2}$ is limiting reagent.

$\therefore$ Number of moles of $NH_{3}$ produced = 2 $\times$ 100 = 200

Mass of $NH_{3}$ produced = 200 × 17 = 3400 gm
